ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Questions below refer to the synthetic pathway of the RNA pyrimidine cytidine 5'-triphosphate (CTP). This pathway begins with the condensation of two small molecules by the enzyme aspartate transcarbamylase (ATCase). This enzymatic phenomenon is an example of what type of regulation?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the “Regulation of CTP biosynthesis” pathway, with carbamyl phosphate and aspartic acid at the starting point, entering subsequent synthesis steps under catalysis by aspartate transcarbamylase (ATCase), and the final product is cytidine 5'-triphosphate (CTP). On the left side of the figure there is a feedback line labeled “High CTP,” returning from near the final product CTP to the ATCase-catalyzed step at the start of the pathway, and pointing to this early step with an inhibition symbol. Then reason: The stem asks what type of regulation this enzyme regulation phenomenon belongs to. The final product CTP of the pathway, when at high concentration, inhibits the early enzyme ATCase in the same biosynthetic pathway, which fits the biochemical definition of “the final product inhibits an earlier step,” therefore it is feedback inhibition.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual pathway: the image shows CTP as the final product and a labeled “High CTP” inhibitory feedback line pointing back to the ATCase-catalyzed first condensation step. Then connect this with the text, which asks what type of regulation this enzymatic phenomenon represents. Apply the biochemical rule that a pathway product inhibiting an earlier enzyme in the same pathway is feedback inhibition. Therefore answer: feedback inhibition.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the pathway diagram’s regulatory arrow directly: identify the product-to-enzyme inhibitory loop rather than relying only on the enzyme name or memorized ATCase facts.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the CTP biosynthesis diagram: carbamyl phosphate and aspartic acid enter the first step catalyzed by aspartate transcarbamylase (ATCase), and the final product cytidine 5'-triphosphate (CTP) is shown at the bottom. A line labeled “High CTP” loops back from the product end to the ATCase step and ends with an inhibitory bar, indicating inhibition of that early enzyme by accumulated CTP.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to identify the relevant enzyme and event: ATCase catalyzes the initial condensation in the synthetic pathway, and the task is to name the regulation type.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In metabolic pathways, when the end product accumulates and inhibits an enzyme catalyzing an early step in its own synthesis, this is called feedback inhibition, specifically end-product negative regulation.
